(CNN) -- Dozens of Defense Department personnel are actively engaged in fighting the wildfires raging in Southern California, Pentagon officials said Tuesday, and thousands more National Guard and active-duty military personnel are available to help. The Rice fire, east of Camp Pendleton, caused the evacuation of the Fallbrook community. Paul McHale, assistant secretary of defense for homeland defense, said that 12 Defense Department firefighting teams, with 12 engines, are already working the blazes and more than 17,000 National Guardsmen are potentially available if needed. In addition, he said, 550 Marines from Camp Pendleton are preparing to deploy to the fire area. "All of the aid that we provide is the result of a request ... from the state," McHale said. "However, we have been very proactive in independently preparing those capabilities for the possibility of such requests, and we have reached out early to state officials." California Gov. Arnold Schwarzenegger has already called up 1,500 National Guard troops, including more than 200 taken from border duty to help with supplies and security at San Diego's Qualcomm Stadium and DelMar Fairgrounds and Racetrack, where thousands of evacuated residents are taking shelter. Schwarzenegger also requested and received from the federal government six "modular airborne fire fighting systems" units -- which are C-130s that drop water and fire suppressant on the blazes.  Watch California Gov. Arnold Schwarzenegger talk about the crisis » . The Pentagon provided 11 helicopters equipped with water buckets to fight the fires, McHale said. Aerial attacks on the fires, however, have been minimal because of high Santa Ana winds with gusts approaching 70 mph. In an effort to make room for more civilians who have had to evacuate their homes, sailors stationed in Southern California are abandoning their barracks. "Orders have been given to all sailors ashore in barracks to move to shipboard billeting to provide room for evacuees," said a Tuesday statement released by the U.S. military. Only essential personnel are requested to report to duty at Naval Base San Diego, Naval Amphibious Base in Coronado, and Naval Air Station in El Centro. Those bases have also set up cots and tents for evacuees. Also, the Navy has offered an Aegis cruiser, a guided missile destroyer, and two fast frigates to support evacuation efforts. Meanwhile, the Pentagon designated March Air Reserve Base as the primary staging area for medical and relief supplies coordinated by the Federal Emergency Management Agency, McHale said. And some 100 California National Guard medical personnel are helping alleviate "critical staffing shortfalls" at the San Diego Veterans Center, whose hospital staff are under voluntary and mandatory evacuation orders. The fires are also having a direct effect on military personnel -- McHale said 1,400 Navy personnel and their families have been forced to evacuate, and Camp Pendleton ordered 3,000 Marines to evacuate because of the fire, the Pentagon announced Tuesday evening. In all, the military has about Video 20 facilities around the San Diego area.  E-mail to a friend .

(CNN) — Pentagon officials said Tuesday that dozens of Defense Department workers are already involved in battling the wildfires burning across Southern California, while thousands of additional National Guard and active-duty troops remain ready to assist if called upon.

The Rice fire, located east of Camp Pendleton, forced residents of Fallbrook to evacuate.

Paul McHale, the assistant secretary of defense for homeland defense, said 12 Defense Department fire crews, using 12 fire engines, were already helping fight the flames. He added that more than 17,000 National Guard members could be made available if necessary. Another 550 Marines from Camp Pendleton, he said, were getting ready to move into the fire zone.

McHale said any military assistance is provided only after a request from the state. Still, he noted that the Defense Department had taken early steps on its own to prepare resources in case such requests came, and had contacted state officials in advance.

California Gov. Arnold Schwarzenegger has activated 1,500 National Guard troops. That number includes more than 200 troops pulled from border assignments to assist with supplies and security at San Diego’s Qualcomm Stadium and the Del Mar Fairgrounds and Racetrack, where thousands of evacuees have taken refuge.

Schwarzenegger also asked the federal government for six modular airborne firefighting system units, and the request was granted. These systems are mounted on C-130 aircraft and are used to drop water and fire retardant on wildfires.

McHale said the Pentagon also supplied 11 helicopters fitted with water buckets for firefighting operations. However, aircraft have been used only sparingly because strong Santa Ana winds have produced gusts nearing 70 mph.

To create additional space for displaced civilians, sailors based in Southern California are leaving their barracks. A U.S. military statement released Tuesday said all sailors housed in barracks on shore had been ordered to move to sleeping quarters aboard ships so evacuees could use the barracks space.

Only essential personnel were asked to report for duty at Naval Base San Diego, Naval Amphibious Base Coronado, and Naval Air Station El Centro. Those installations have also put up cots and tents for evacuees.

The Navy has additionally made available an Aegis cruiser, a guided-missile destroyer, and two fast frigates to help with evacuation operations.

At the same time, McHale said the Pentagon selected March Air Reserve Base as the main staging site for medical and emergency supplies being coordinated by the Federal Emergency Management Agency.

About 100 medical personnel from the California National Guard are also helping address severe staffing shortages at the San Diego Veterans Center, where hospital employees are subject to both voluntary and mandatory evacuation orders.

The fires have also directly affected members of the military. McHale said 1,400 Navy personnel and their families had been ordered to leave their homes. The Pentagon announced Tuesday evening that Camp Pendleton had ordered 3,000 Marines to evacuate because of the fire.

Altogether, the military operates about 20 facilities in the San Diego area.

Officials emphasized that the military does not take over wildfire operations. # Rice Fire near Camp Pendleton prompts evacuations in Fallbrook as military assets deploy

**FALLBROOK, California** — A fast-moving wildfire burning near Camp Pendleton has forced evacuations in parts of Fallbrook, as local, state and federal agencies mount a large-scale response that includes military aircraft, personnel, ships and medical support.

The blaze, identified as the **Rice Fire**, ignited near the boundary of the sprawling Marine Corps base in northern San Diego County and quickly raised concerns as winds pushed smoke and flames toward nearby communities. Officials issued evacuation orders and warnings for areas around Fallbrook, urging residents to leave early and avoid waiting until conditions worsened.

Emergency officials said firefighters were battling difficult terrain, shifting winds and dry vegetation. Crews from Cal Fire, local fire departments and military firefighting units were working to establish containment lines and protect homes, infrastructure and base facilities.

## Evacuations ordered in Fallbrook

Authorities directed residents in affected zones of Fallbrook to evacuate immediately, while other neighborhoods were placed under evacuation warnings. Emergency shelters were opened for displaced residents, with accommodations for families, pets and people with medical needs.

Officials urged evacuees to take essential documents, medications, emergency supplies and pets, and to avoid roadways being used by fire crews and emergency vehicles.

“Leaving early saves lives,” emergency managers said in public alerts, warning that fire conditions can change rapidly.

Because of the fire’s proximity to Camp Pendleton, military resources were mobilized to support civilian firefighting efforts. Aircraft assigned to the response included helicopters capable of water drops, aerial reconnaissance and emergency transport.

Military personnel were also deployed to assist with logistics, perimeter security, evacuation support and coordination with local incident commanders. Base fire crews worked alongside civilian agencies to defend military installations and nearby communities.

Officials said the use of military aircraft was being coordinated through established mutual-aid channels, ensuring that flight operations did not interfere with civilian air tankers, helicopters or emergency medical flights.

## Ships and medical teams placed on standby

Naval and Marine Corps assets in the region were also activated or placed on standby to provide additional support. Ships offshore or in nearby ports were prepared to assist with command-and-control functions, communications support, transport and medical capacity if needed.

Officials emphasized that the medical deployment was precautionary but necessary given the size of the response and the potential for rapid fire growth.

## Smoke impacts and air quality concerns

Smoke from the Rice Fire drifted across portions of northern San Diego County, prompting air quality advisories. Health officials urged residents — especially children, older adults and people with asthma, heart disease or other respiratory conditions — to remain indoors, keep windows closed and use filtered air when possible.

People in smoky areas were advised to avoid strenuous outdoor activity and wear properly fitted N95 masks if they had to be outside.

## Firefighters brace for changing conditions

Additional firefighting resources were requested as officials prepared for the possibility of extended operations into the evening and overnight.

Authorities said the cause of the Rice Fire remains under investigation.

Residents affected by the fire were urged to check official updates from **San Diego County emergency services, Cal Fire, Camp Pendleton, local law enforcement and evacuation alert systems** for the latest information on evacuation zones, shelter locations and road closures.
